Performance Audit of My Cat Explorer Page

Week 9 · Shrestha Puja · Student ID 202537250 · Audits run on 4 November 2026

1. What I tested

I audited my Cat Explorer page from Week 6, CatExplorer.html. I used Lighthouse in Chrome DevTools with only the Performance category selected and the device set to Mobile. My home page already scored 100 on Desktop and 99 on Mobile, so it gave me nothing to improve. The Cat Explorer page loads cat photos from an outside API, which made it a better page to test.

2. Initial audit: 75 / 100

Almost the whole problem was Largest Contentful Paint (LCP), which measures how long the biggest item on the screen takes to appear. It was 11.2 seconds. Lighthouse also estimated 8,380 KiB of possible savings under "Improve image delivery" and 5,834 KiB under "Use efficient cache lifetimes".

3. Diagnosis

Reading my code, I found the cause. The page builds 9 breed cards, and each card has a photo that comes straight from TheCatAPI at its original size. The browser started downloading all nine at the same time, even though only one or two are visible on a phone screen. The photos competed with each other, so the main image arrived very late. The photos were also far larger than the roughly 350 pixels my cards display.

4. Fixes

Fix 1: lazy loading, with priority on the first photo

I made only the first photo load immediately, and told the browser to wait on the other eight until the person scrolls near them.

if (index === 0) {
    photo.setAttribute("fetchpriority", "high");
} else {
    photo.loading = "lazy";
}

Fix 2: preconnect hints

I told the browser which outside servers it would need, so it can open those connections early.

<link rel="preconnect" href="https://api.thecatapi.com">
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://wsrv.nl">

Fix 3: smaller, compressed photos

After Fix 1, Lighthouse still reported large image savings, because each photo was still a full-size original. I now request a resized, compressed WebP copy of each photo through a free image service (wsrv.nl). If that service ever fails, the page falls back to the original photo, so cards never go blank.

function optimizedImage(url) {
    return "https://wsrv.nl/?url=" + encodeURIComponent(url) +
        "&w=700&h=420&fit=cover&output=webp&q=70";
}

function setPhoto(photo, url) {
    photo.onerror = function () {
        photo.onerror = null;
        photo.src = url;   // fall back to the original photo
    };
    photo.src = optimizedImage(url);
}

This fix depends on a third-party service, which is a trade-off: if that service were slow or removed, the page would rely on the fallback and lose the speed gain.

6. Which change mattered most

The biggest single improvement was to LCP. Lazy loading with a priority on the first photo cut it from 11.2 s to 1.3 s, and resizing the photos brought it to 0.5 s. Resizing also appears to have helped the other metrics: Total Blocking Time went from 290 ms to 20 ms and Speed Index from 3.7 s to 0.7 s. Lighthouse's "Improve image delivery" estimate fell from 8,380 KiB to 4,889 KiB after Fix 1, and later to 25 KiB in one of my final runs. Because scores change between runs, I can say which fix helped most, but not give exact points for each one.

7. Limits and honesty about the results

Lighthouse scores on this page varied a lot between runs, even with the same code. After Fix 1 I got 92, 88 and 72, and for the final version I got 96 and 100. So the 100 is my best run, not a guarantee. The variation probably comes from the simulated slow phone and from waiting on TheCatAPI's server, which my code does not control. I also did not repeat the "before" audit, so the 75 is a single run.

8. What I learned

I learned that the biggest item on a page can dominate its performance score, and on my page that was a photo. Photos from an outside API can be much larger than the space they are shown in, and requesting a smaller copy makes a large difference. I also learned that a single Lighthouse run is not enough, because scores move around, so repeating the audit and reporting every result gives a more honest picture.

9. Tools and help

I ran all of the Lighthouse audits and tested the changes myself. I used an AI assistant to help me understand the Lighthouse results and to write the code changes, and I checked the results on my live page.
